SMTO-SKL-0133 — Slack sent back an answer SMTO couldn't use

GUID: 649f89a2-25b3-55bc-a353-fb632a09dfb6
Slug: slack-provider-response-invalid
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • Slack replied, but the reply wasn't in the form SMTO expected or didn't match what was asked for, so SMTO didn't use it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you asked SMTO to post, upload or change something, check in Slack whether it already happened. SMTO can't tell from a reply it couldn't read whether the change went through.
  2. If it was only a read, such as listing messages or files, ask the Agent for it once more. A one-off bad reply from Slack often doesn't happen again.
  3. If it happens again, select Copy error details. The copied details identify this exact failure, so the person who manages SMTO can look it up.

What success looks like

  • The request returns normal results.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO; this may need an SMTO update. Don't keep repeating posts or uploads while it's failing.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Slack Web API or file-transfer response failed validation (malformed JSON, unexpected object or list shape, oversized page, a non-Slack transfer URL, or a returned resource ID that differs from the request).

What this means

  • Slack response/transfer URL parsing, object/list projection or exact resource identity validation fails; malformed post-dispatch writes have a separate unknown-outcome path. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Slack response/transfer URL parsing, object/list projection or exact resource identity validation fails; malformed post-dispatch writes have a separate unknown-outcome path.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the failed shape, bound, URL or exact channel/message identity check.

How to fix it

  • Record the error_id and inspect the exact resource with a separate read. Unexpected provider data never proves a write succeeded, so check Slack before any repeated write; a persistent failure suggests a Slack API change that needs a fix in skills/slack/projection.py or service.py.
  • Preserve the error ID and inspect the exact resource; unexpected provider data cannot establish safe write replay.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported response validates before it is used as evidence.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
